We also included a current subprocessor inventory (Subprocessor_List_20260928.xlsx). Our legal would like to align on whether Redwood would allow a shorter window (45 days) with an escalated review for high-risk categories.

Jordan — thanks for the redline and the list. Quick notes from my side:

- Redwood's standard public customer notice window for new subprocessors is 45 days. For enterprise customers we can extend to 60 days on a case-by-case basis tied to contract language.
- Objection process today: customer submits objection -> we evaluate classification (high/medium/low risk) -> if high, we pause onboarding and engage remediation or mitigation; if unresolved, we facilitate vendor removal or other technical/workflow mitigations. Timeline target is 30 days for initial triage, 60 days to resolution for high-risk objections.

I dragged in Neha (privacy lead) and Laura (legal ops) to confirm if we can accept 60 days broadly or need to link to customer tier. Karthik — can you review the proposed fallbacks in §7.3 and advise if the technical mitigations are feasible within the 60 day window?

Ben

Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + subprocessor list and notification window

Thanks Ben. Quick internal alignment before we send a formal counter:

- Notification window: we can confirm 45 days standard; we will accept 60 days for customers that sign the enterprise SOW (i.e., contract-level concession). We should avoid making 60 days a standard for all hosted customers because it increases exposure.
- Objection workflow: propose the following formal steps to include in the DPA redline:
  1) Customer submits objection via support/legal channel (we'll include an email alias).
  2) Redwood acknowledges within 3 business days and assigns an internal risk lead.
  3) Triage completed within 20 business days with proposed mitigations or acceptance.
  4) If mitigation not possible, offer contract-level options (additional controls, limited data scope, termination for that processing path).

- For high-risk processors (security, identity, payments), we will treat objections as escalatable and aim for 60 calendar days to final remediation. For lower risk, 30 days should be sufficient.

Laura — can you draft precise language for §7.3 and add an optional clause that allows extension by mutual written agreement? Jordan — if you can confirm which processors on the attached list you consider high-risk, that will speed things up.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: DPA redlines + subprocessor list and notification window

Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is Redwood's proposed clean DPA language plus an appendix that codifies the objection workflow (we marked it as §7.3.2). Highlights:

- Notification window: Standard 45 calendar days; enterprise customers can elect a 60-day window via SOW.
- Objection process: mirrors what Neha proposed; we made timelines explicit (ack 3 business days, triage 20 business days, remediation 60 days for high risk).
- Fallbacks: if remediation fails for high-risk processors, we offer (a) additional contractual commitments (e.g., restricted processing only), (b) assistance to move data/terminate that processing path, or (c) mutual termination of the specific processing activity.

We also included an e-sign path: once Acme confirms risk categories for the items in Subprocessor_List_20260928.xlsx we can push the DocuSign envelope. Link below.

DocuSign (pre-auth): https://docusign.com/envelope/12345-abcdef

Please reply with: (1) list of items you deem high-risk, and (2) whether Acme will accept the enterprise-tier SOW approach for a 60-day window (if required). We can get this executed within ~2 business days after you confirm.

Thanks,
